scenarios.brief: The lead vehicle brake-checks the ego briefly then resumes.
scenarios.name: Lead brake-check then release
scenarios.whyNot: The lead vehicle does not visibly perform a sharp braking pause followed by a resumption; it continues along its turning and crossing path. The ego's speed changes do not establish that the lead brake-checked.
scenarios.whatISee: The red lead vehicle approaches from the right, follows the junction around, and continues across the ego's path while the blue ego slows and changes direction. The lead remains in motion through the sequence and is later ahead to the left rather than visibly stopping and restarting.

scenarios.brief: A slower lead vehicle is encountered at closing speed (Euro NCAP CCRm).
scenarios.name: Hidden slow lead vehicle at closing speed
scenarios.whatISee: The blue ego travels toward a red vehicle that is ahead on the curving roadway, initially at a higher speed and then decelerates substantially as it closes on the red vehicle. The red vehicle continues ahead around the bend, while the ego follows it at progressively lower speed through the closest-approach frame and afterward.

scenarios.brief: The lead vehicle brakes hard in flowing traffic; the ego follows at a normal headway with a human reaction delay.
scenarios.name: Unexpected hard stop in flowing traffic
scenarios.whyNot: The frames do not show the lead moving and then braking sharply; it appears already stopped or moving very slowly as the ego approaches and brakes.
scenarios.whatISee: The ego travels toward a red lead vehicle that is already near the junction curve ahead. The ego then decelerates from 62 km/h to a stop while closing to a short gap behind the lead, which remains essentially in the same position.

scenarios.brief: The lead vehicle in the ego lane is already stopped; the ego closes on it and must avoid a rear-end.
scenarios.name: Blind stopped lead rear-end avoidance
scenarios.whyNot: The red vehicle is initially on a separate intersecting lane rather than already stopped in the ego's lane; the ego only converges toward it while turning through the junction.
scenarios.whatISee: The blue ego travels rightward past a stationary yellow roadside box truck while the red stoppedLead remains on a separate vertical road at the junction. The ego slows and turns toward that road, coming very close to the stationary red vehicle at the marked closest approach without contacting it.

scenarios.brief: Stop-and-go traffic: the lead repeatedly stops and moves off.
scenarios.name: Survivable repeated stop-and-go lead
scenarios.whyNot: The frames show the ego slowing during a close approach to a lead vehicle, but they do not show the lead repeatedly stopping and moving off.
scenarios.whatISee: The red lead vehicle appears ahead of the blue ego and follows the road as it bends left and downhill. The ego slows sharply from 62 kph to 9 and then 3 kph while approaching it, but the lead does not visibly make repeated stop-and-move cycles; it continues along the bend.

scenarios.brief: The ego is tailgated while the lead ahead brakes.
scenarios.name: Delayed tailgater behind an unexpectedly braking lead
scenarios.whyNot: Although a tailgating vehicle is present initially and there is a lead vehicle ahead later, the lead is not shown moving and then braking sharply; it appears to be turning or continuing slowly along the bend.
scenarios.whatISee: A red vehicle starts behind the blue ego in the same roadway, labeled as the tailgater. Later, a red lead vehicle is ahead near the right-hand bend; the ego slows from 53 kph to 8 kph and closes toward it while the lead turns along the bend.

scenarios.brief: The ego judges a gap to overtake with oncoming traffic.
scenarios.name: Hidden-gap overtake with late oncoming traffic
scenarios.whyNot: Oncoming traffic and a slow lead are present, but the ego never actually overtakes or crosses into the opposing lane; it remains behind the lead vehicle.
scenarios.whatISee: The ego approaches a slow lead vehicle while an oncoming vehicle comes around the curve from the opposite approach. The ego slows substantially and follows the lead through the junction, without moving across into the opposing lane to overtake.

scenarios.brief: A third party overtakes toward the ego in the oncoming lane.
scenarios.name: Late oncoming overtake lane intrusion
scenarios.whyNot: The red vehicle is already ahead of the ego and does not visibly perform an overtake by crossing into the ego's lane; it simply continues along the roadway while the ego brakes and turns away.
scenarios.whatISee: The red vehicle is already ahead of the blue ego on the vertical roadway and remains in essentially the same path as the ego as the gap closes. The ego slows sharply and then turns right at the junction while the red vehicle continues onward, producing a close pass/conflict.

scenarios.brief: A conflict occurs in a parking aisle at low speed.
scenarios.name: Late reversing vehicle in an occluded parking aisle
scenarios.whatISee: The ego drives along the parking aisle while a red reversing van emerges from beside/behind a parked vehicle and comes into close proximity ahead of the ego. The van then moves away relative to the ego, with no collision shown.

scenarios.brief: A vehicle backs out of a parking space into the ego path.
scenarios.name: Late reverse-out from kerbside parking
scenarios.whyNot: The red vehicle is revealed on the roadway but there is no visible parking space or maneuver showing it backing out of one; it appears already aligned with and traveling along the road rather than entering the ego path from a parking space.
scenarios.whatISee: Initially the red vehicle is hidden behind the yellow blocker. It then becomes visible on the lower roadway ahead of the ego, remains aligned with that roadway as the ego closes to the closest approach, and is behind the ego by the next frame.

scenarios.brief: A double-parked delivery vehicle blocks the ego lane.
scenarios.name: Late-revealed double-parked delivery truck
scenarios.whatISee: The blue ego vehicle travels toward a bend and approaches a stationary red delivery truck positioned in the roadway ahead. It progressively slows from 59 kph to about 3 kph at the closest approach, with a yellow kerbside-parked van nearby.

scenarios.brief: A ball rolls out followed by a child in a school zone.
scenarios.name: Ball then hidden child at roadside school-like approach
scenarios.whatISee: A yellow truck initially hides a ball and a small red child actor near the roadway. The ball emerges first, followed by the child, while the blue ego vehicle approaches and slows sharply from 43 to 16 kph at closest approach before continuing past.

scenarios.brief: Chaotic school drop-off with vehicles and children.
scenarios.name: Late-hidden school drop-off child dart
scenarios.whatISee: The ego approaches a junction where several drop-off vehicles are clustered and moving or positioned around the roadway. A child is present near the roadway and comes very close to the ego's path at the marked closest approach, after which the ego continues away.

scenarios.brief: A vehicle ahead loses traction on a friction patch.
scenarios.name: Lead vehicle loses traction on a friction patch
scenarios.whyNot: The red vehicle does not visibly undergo a demonstrable traction loss on a distinct friction patch; it instead appears to rotate or cross the ego's path. The roadway shown provides no clear friction-patch event linking the vehicle's motion to reduced grip.
scenarios.whatISee: The ego travels along the straight roadway and approaches a red vehicle that appears ahead and angled across the roadway. The red vehicle rotates and moves across and then away from the ego's path while the ego slows, reaching the marked closest approach.

scenarios.brief: A third-party vehicle spins into the ego path.
scenarios.name: Third-party vehicle spins into ego path
scenarios.whyNot: The red vehicle does enter a hazardous area near the ego path, but it does not visibly spin; it remains oriented along its roadway while crossing or merging near the ego.
scenarios.whatISee: The blue ego vehicle follows the curving road toward the junction while the red challenger approaches along the adjacent/crossing roadway. The challenger moves into the ego's vicinity and passes very close across the ego's trajectory at the marked closest approach, but its heading remains generally consistent rather than visibly rotating.

scenarios.brief: Pedestrians occupy the carriageway unexpectedly.
scenarios.name: Blind-side pedestrian walk-in from carriageway occlusion
scenarios.whatISee: The ego drives toward a box truck and a pedestrian ahead, with the pedestrian positioned on the carriageway near the truck. The pedestrian remains in the roadway through the closest-approach frames, creating a near conflict, and is then left behind as the ego continues.

scenarios.brief: A truck ahead sheds part of its load.
scenarios.name: Hidden load shed from lead truck
scenarios.whatISee: A truck appears ahead of the ego, traveling in the same lane, with a separate piece of load visible behind it. The detached load remains in the ego's path as the ego rapidly slows from 62 kph to 1 kph by the closest approach.

scenarios.brief: A vehicle drifts from the adjacent lane into the ego blind spot.
scenarios.name: Blind-spot late adjacent-lane cut-in
scenarios.whyNot: The red vehicle begins ahead of the ego in its lane rather than in an adjacent lane, and its late movement is away toward the adjacent lane rather than a cut-in into the ego's lane or blind spot.
scenarios.whatISee: The red vehicle is already ahead of the blue ego vehicle in the same leftward lane throughout the early frames. Near the closest approach it turns or drifts downward toward the adjacent lane while the ego vehicle brakes sharply, but it does not come across from an adjacent lane into the ego lane.

scenarios.brief: A lead vehicle cuts out and reveals a stopped vehicle ahead.
scenarios.name: Lead clears stopped-car reveal
scenarios.whatISee: The red lead vehicle is initially ahead of the ego in the same lane, with a stopped red vehicle farther ahead and largely hidden behind it. The lead then moves laterally out of the ego's lane, revealing the stopped vehicle directly ahead as the ego slows toward it.

scenarios.brief: A vehicle crosses the ego lane to reach an exit.
scenarios.name: Late opposing cut-in across ego lane
scenarios.whyNot: The red vehicle remains in its own opposing lane and does not cross into the ego's lane; the ego turns onto and then off the vertical road without the required vehicle cut-across occurring.
scenarios.whatISee: The blue ego vehicle travels along the upper road and turns onto the vertical road, while the red vehicle approaches upward on that vertical road. They pass very close to one another near the marked closest approach, after which the ego turns off onto the lower road and the red vehicle continues upward.

scenarios.brief: The ego lane drops and traffic must merge late.
scenarios.name: Late cut-in at a disappearing lane
scenarios.whyNot: Although the vehicles come dangerously close, the red vehicle does not actually cross into the ego's lane and merge ahead; it stays on its own route.
scenarios.whatISee: The ego and the red vehicle approach the junction with the red vehicle closing from behind in the adjacent lane. They reach a close approach, after which the ego continues onto the lower horizontal roadway while the red vehicle remains on the separate diagonal/left roadway rather than merging ahead of the ego.

scenarios.brief: A merging vehicle takes a gap that collapses.
scenarios.name: Late aggressive merge into a collapsing gap
scenarios.whyNot: The red vehicle never clearly moves across into the ego's lane or takes a gap that subsequently collapses; it stays in its own lane while the ego approaches and passes.
scenarios.whatISee: The red vehicle is ahead and to the side of the blue ego vehicle, then remains in a neighboring lane as the ego draws alongside and later passes it. At the marked closest approach they are near each other, but the red vehicle does not visibly cross into the ego's lane; later it is seen near the junction ahead.

scenarios.brief: A vehicle pulls out of a parking space directly into the ego lane.
scenarios.name: Blind parking-space pullout into ego lane
scenarios.whyNot: The red vehicle initially pulls into the neighboring lane rather than directly into the ego's lane; it only later turns across the ego's path at the junction.
scenarios.whatISee: The blue ego vehicle approaches while the red pullout vehicle emerges ahead in the adjacent lane beside the parked vehicles. The red vehicle then turns left across the ego's path at the junction, causing the ego to brake to a stop as the red vehicle continues away.

scenarios.brief: A vehicle merges from an on-ramp into the ego lane.
scenarios.name: Late aggressive ramp merge into ego lane
scenarios.whyNot: The red vehicle stays in its own adjacent lane and never visibly moves across into the ego lane.
scenarios.whatISee: The red merger vehicle travels forward alongside the blue ego vehicle, remaining in the lane to the ego's left as the roadway continues. It comes close alongside/ahead at the marked closest approach, then is no longer visible, without visibly crossing into the ego's lane.

scenarios.brief: Two vehicles weave across each other around the ego.
scenarios.name: Late reciprocal cut-in weave around ego
scenarios.whyNot: Only one red vehicle is shown making the substantive crossing maneuver near the ego; the other red vehicle seen initially does not participate in a demonstrated weave around the ego.
scenarios.whatISee: The ego approaches the junction while a red vehicle travels around the junction and then moves laterally across the ego's path, ending alongside and very close to it. Another red vehicle is visible initially on the cross street, but it does not visibly weave across the ego with the other vehicle.

scenarios.brief: Two vehicles negotiate an all-way stop and both proceed.
scenarios.name: All-way-stop cross-traffic violation
scenarios.whyNot: The vehicles do proceed, but they do not visibly negotiate the intersection as an all-way stop: neither makes a stop, and the red vehicle simply turns ahead of the ego.
scenarios.whatISee: The blue ego vehicle follows the red vehicle east toward an intersection. The red vehicle turns onto the northbound road while the ego slows sharply, then also turns and continues northbound behind it; neither vehicle visibly stops at the intersection.

scenarios.brief: An emergency vehicle crosses the junction against the ego.
scenarios.name: Ambulance cuts across an uncontrolled junction
scenarios.whatISee: The ego approaches the junction while an ambulance enters on the cross street and travels through the intersection. At the marked closest approach, the ambulance passes directly across the ego's path, then continues away as the ego proceeds.

scenarios.brief: The ego turns left across an oncoming motorcycle.
scenarios.name: Arrival-timed oncoming motorcycle across ego left turn
scenarios.whyNot: The motorcycle stays in its opposing lane and the ego does not turn across its path; they pass each other in adjacent lanes.
scenarios.whatISee: The blue ego vehicle enters the horizontal roadway and proceeds to the right, remaining in its lane. A red motorcycle approaches from the right in the opposing lane, passes the ego at the marked closest approach, and then continues away to the left.

scenarios.brief: The ego turns left across an oncoming through vehicle at a junction.
scenarios.name: Late non-yielding oncoming vehicle during left turn
scenarios.whyNot: The red vehicle does not continue straight through the junction; it turns onto the cross street. Thus the required oncoming-through movement is missing, even though the vehicles come into close conflict.
scenarios.whatISee: The ego approaches the junction and slows as a red vehicle comes toward it on the opposing approach. The red vehicle then turns left around the junction onto the cross street, while the ego also completes a left turn after the close approach.

scenarios.brief: A vehicle enters the junction late against the signal.
scenarios.name: Late control-violating opposing left turn
scenarios.whatISee: The red vehicle approaches the junction, turns diagonally across the ego's path, and comes very close as the ego slows sharply. It then continues away through the junction while the ego proceeds onto the intersecting road.

scenarios.brief: A circulating vehicle cuts across the ego exit path.
scenarios.name: Late circulating vehicle cuts across exit
scenarios.whatISee: The blue ego approaches and begins to take its exit while the red circulating challenger arrives from the right and traverses the exit roadway in front of it. At closest approach the ego slows sharply from about 30 km/h to 10 km/h, after which the challenger continues away and the vehicles separate.

scenarios.brief: An adult crosses mid-block into the ego path.
scenarios.name: Hidden adult midblock crossing
scenarios.whyNot: The adult is present near the roadside but does not visibly cross into the ego path; the apparent conflict results from the ego approaching a stationary roadside pedestrian.
scenarios.whatISee: The ego approaches the junction and slows as an adult stands beside the roadway near the ego's path. The adult remains in essentially the same roadside position while the ego passes close by and then continues away; there is no visible movement of the adult across the road.

scenarios.brief: A pedestrian emerges in front of a stopped bus.
scenarios.name: Pedestrian emerges beyond stopped bus
scenarios.whyNot: The pedestrian is already visible at the front/side of the bus in the first frame and does not transition from behind the bus or from an occluded position into the road.
scenarios.whatISee: The ego approaches a stopped bus with the pedestrian already visible at the bus's front/right side. The ego slows sharply as it closes on the pedestrian, reaches the closest approach, and then continues past while the pedestrian remains near the bus.

scenarios.brief: A pedestrian crosses from the far side (NCAP CPFA).
scenarios.name: Hidden far-side pedestrian crossing
scenarios.whyNot: There is no pedestrian crossing from the far side in any frame; the visible actors are box trucks, so the required pedestrian-crossing mechanism does not occur.
scenarios.whatISee: The blue ego vehicle approaches a junction and slows as box trucks are present on the far-side roadway. It reaches a closest approach beside the trucks, then continues through and away from the junction; no pedestrian is visible or enters the road.

scenarios.brief: A pedestrian crosses from the nearside close to the ego (NCAP CPNA).
scenarios.name: Late nearside pedestrian emergence behind roadside truck
scenarios.whyNot: The pedestrian is already present near the roadway and appears to remain alongside or travel along the vertical road; there is no clear nearside-to-road crossing into the ego's lane.
scenarios.whatISee: The ego travels east toward an intersection and slows sharply while a pedestrian is already visible on the adjoining vertical roadway, alongside a box truck. The ego then turns north and comes very close to the pedestrian at closest approach, before accelerating away; the pedestrian does not visibly enter the ego's lane from the roadside.

scenarios.brief: A group of pedestrians crosses together.
scenarios.name: Hidden pedestrian group crossing
scenarios.whyNot: The pedestrians are already clustered in or alongside the roadway and remain ahead of the ego; the frames do not show them entering from one side and traversing across the road together.
scenarios.whatISee: The ego drives toward the junction, where a clustered group of three pedestrians is present in the roadway ahead. As the ego turns onto the curved road, the pedestrians remain together ahead of it and the ego slows sharply from 52 kph to 7 kph at closest approach.

scenarios.brief: A pedestrian steps out from behind a stopped vehicle in the adjacent lane.
scenarios.name: Pedestrian emerges from adjacent-lane stopped vehicle
scenarios.whyNot: The frames do not show the pedestrian emerging from behind the vehicle or entering the road; the pedestrian is already visible ahead/right of it and remains essentially stationary.
scenarios.whatISee: The ego vehicle approaches a stopped red vehicle in its lane and brakes from 52 kph to 2 kph. A pedestrian is visible ahead and to the right of the stopped vehicle from 4 seconds onward, but remains in that roadside/junction position rather than visibly stepping out into the road.

scenarios.brief: A pedestrian walks behind a reversing vehicle.
scenarios.name: Reversing van conceals trailing pedestrian
scenarios.whyNot: The pedestrian does not enter the road from behind the van; it stays alongside the vehicle at the roadside. The actual conflict is between the ego and the reversing van.
scenarios.whatISee: The ego approaches a red van that is reversing near the junction, and the van comes very close to the ego at the marked closest approach. A pedestrian is visible beside the van along the roadside, but remains outside the ego's lane and does not emerge into the road behind the van.

scenarios.brief: A cyclist crosses from the nearside close to the ego (NCAP CBNA).
scenarios.name: Hidden nearside cyclist crossing
scenarios.whyNot: The cyclist does not cross laterally from the nearside; it travels along the roadway toward and past the ego, producing a close oncoming pass instead.
scenarios.whatISee: The cyclist appears ahead of the ego and approaches along the roadway in the opposite direction. It passes very close alongside the ego at the marked closest approach, then falls behind as the ego continues and accelerates.

scenarios.brief: A cyclist is right-hooked by a turning vehicle ahead of the ego.
scenarios.name: Late right-hook across cyclist
scenarios.whyNot: Although a turning vehicle and a cyclist are present, the frames do not show the vehicle right-hooking the cyclist or crossing the cyclist's path.
scenarios.whatISee: The red vehicle starts ahead of the blue ego in the same lane, then turns through the junction while the ego follows and comes very close to it at the marked closest approach. The red vehicle continues away, and a cyclist is only visible later on the roadway; no frame shows the turning vehicle crossing the cyclist's path or hooking it.

scenarios.brief: A parked car door opens into a cyclist who swerves into the ego lane.
scenarios.name: Late cyclist dooring swerve into ego path
scenarios.whyNot: The cyclist does enter the ego's path, but no parked-car door opening into the cyclist is shown, so the required causal mechanism is missing.
scenarios.whatISee: The ego approaches a stationary parked car and a cyclist near the car. The cyclist moves into the ego vehicle's path, creating a close conflict, and the ego slows and then turns away while the parked car remains stationary.

scenarios.brief: An e-scooter enters the ego lane from the footway.
scenarios.name: Late e-scooter footway entry into ego lane
scenarios.whatISee: The ego approaches the junction while the e-scooter appears at the footway edge. The scooter then moves off the footway into the roadway and across/in front of the ego's path; the ego slows and turns through the junction, reaching close proximity with the scooter as both continue.

scenarios.brief: A stopped bus hides a cyclist from the ego.
scenarios.name: Cyclist emerging from behind stopped bus
scenarios.whyNot: The bus and cyclist do not form the required line-of-sight occlusion: the cyclist remains offset in a separate lane and is not revealed by emerging from behind the stopped bus.
scenarios.whatISee: The ego approaches the junction while a cyclist travels along the crossing road, and a stopped bus is visible ahead on the ego's route. The cyclist later comes alongside or just ahead of the ego in a separate lane while the bus remains stopped, creating a close interaction but not one where the bus blocks the cyclist from the ego.

scenarios.brief: A crest hides a stopped vehicle from the ego.
scenarios.name: Blind crest stopped-vehicle emergence
scenarios.whatISee: Initially the ego is traveling toward the crest and the stopped vehicle is not visible. After the crest, a red stopped vehicle appears ahead in the ego's lane; the ego slows sharply from 58 kph to 26, then 10 and finally 1 kph at closest approach while remaining behind it.

scenarios.brief: A pedestrian steps out from behind a double-parked truck.
scenarios.name: Late pedestrian emergence from double-parked truck
scenarios.whyNot: The pedestrian is visible alongside the stopped truck but does not show a clear movement from behind it into the ego's lane; the clip depicts a roadside pedestrian conflict rather than a demonstrated dart-out from behind the truck.
scenarios.whatISee: Two stopped trucks occupy the ego's lane ahead. A pedestrian becomes visible beside the downstream truck and remains near its side as the ego approaches, slows sharply, passes the pedestrian, and then continues through the junction.

scenarios.brief: A roadside hedge hides a crossing pedestrian at a corner.
scenarios.name: Hedge-hidden corner pedestrian crossing repaired
scenarios.whyNot: Although the hedge initially obscures the pedestrian, the pedestrian remains at the roadside and never steps out or crosses into the ego's path.
scenarios.whatISee: The ego approaches the corner and slows while a hedge lies between it and a pedestrian standing at the roadside. It passes very close to the stationary pedestrian and then continues around the junction; the pedestrian does not move into the roadway.

scenarios.brief: A vehicle emerges from behind a row of parked cars.
scenarios.name: Hidden kerbside vehicle emerges into ego path
scenarios.whatISee: The blue ego vehicle approaches a row of yellow parked cars along the curved road. A red sedan is initially hidden among or behind the parked row, then becomes visible as it emerges onto the roadway ahead of the ego; the two vehicles continue around the bend with a close approach before separating slightly.

scenarios.brief: Construction occupies part of an intersection with plant, barriers and a flagger.
scenarios.name: Blind intersection workzone with plant, barriers and late flagger
scenarios.whatISee: The ego approaches the junction and slows as a red plant truck turns upward through the intersection, coming alongside and creating a close approach. Yellow construction plant and barriers occupy part of the junction, with a red-ringed flagger stationed beside the barriers throughout.

scenarios.brief: A slow-moving work vehicle occupies the ego lane.
scenarios.name: Late-revealed slow work vehicle in ego lane
scenarios.whatISee: The ego travels along the vertical roadway and a red work vehicle is ahead in the same lane by 6 seconds. The ego closes on it while slowing from 59 kph to 12 kph, reaching closest approach with the work vehicle still occupying the lane ahead.

scenarios.brief: Barriers narrow the ego lane through a work area.
scenarios.name: Work-zone barrier squeeze with late opposing turn intrusion
scenarios.whatISee: The ego travels along the roadway, turns into a narrower vertical road segment, and approaches a line of yellow work barriers running alongside and partly into its path. It passes very close to the barriers at the marked closest approach and then continues forward alongside them.

scenarios.brief: A night work zone with limited conspicuity.
scenarios.name: Night work-zone truck conceals opposing late left turn
scenarios.whyNot: Although a stopped work truck is present, it remains plainly visible and there is no clear depiction of limited conspicuity, nighttime visibility impairment, or an occluding object hiding the hazard.
scenarios.whatISee: The blue ego vehicle approaches an intersection where a yellow stopped work truck is present, then turns onto the cross street and passes near it. A red van is also present near the truck, while the ego slows substantially at the closest approach before continuing past the work-zone vehicles.

scenarios.brief: A work zone shifts the alignment laterally and the ego steers around it.
scenarios.name: Blind work-zone lateral shift around stopped truck
scenarios.whyNot: The frames show the ego approaching and maneuvering around a stationary work-zone obstruction and an oncoming truck, but they do not clearly show the work zone shifting the roadway alignment laterally; the ego mainly slows and passes beside the obstruction.
scenarios.whatISee: The ego approaches a yellow work-zone obstruction while an oncoming red work-zone truck is ahead on the adjacent path. The ego slows sharply, passes to the right of the work-zone area, and comes to a stop or near-stop as it passes the truck.

scenarios.brief: A lane-closure taper forces traffic to merge in front of the ego.
scenarios.name: Late aggressive merge at lane-drop taper
scenarios.whyNot: There is no visible lane-closure taper forcing a lateral merge into the ego's lane; the red vehicle follows a junction/turning route and the conflict results from converging paths rather than a cut-in across the ego's lane.
scenarios.whatISee: The red late_merger travels ahead of the ego on a separate lane, then turns through the junction while the ego approaches from another route. Near the closest-approach frame they become dangerously close, and afterward the red vehicle is ahead of the ego on the continuing road.

scenarios.brief: A road worker steps out of the work area into the live lane.
scenarios.name: Hidden road worker steps into live lane
scenarios.whyNot: The worker does not visibly step out or cross into the live lane; they remain beside the work vehicle/work area throughout the sequence.
scenarios.whatISee: A yellow work vehicle and a red-ringed road worker are visible beside the ego's approach, with the worker remaining next to the work area at the road edge. The ego passes very close to them and then turns through the junction, while the worker does not visibly step across into the live lane.

scenarios.brief: An accident scene partially blocks the ego lane.
scenarios.name: Late-revealed partial-lane accident scene
scenarios.whyNot: The accident vehicles do not partially block the ego lane; they remain in the neighboring lane, so the ego passes them without its lane being obstructed.
scenarios.whatISee: The blue ego approaches an intersection, turns onto the vertical roadway, and then passes close to a stationary disabled sedan and scene SUV. The accident vehicles remain in the adjacent lane while the ego continues in its own lane; a box truck is also stationary near the intersection.

scenarios.brief: An animal crosses into the ego path.
scenarios.name: Blind roadside pedestrian crossing
scenarios.whyNot: No animal is present; the actor crossing near the ego is a pedestrian, so the named animal-crossing mechanism is not realised.
scenarios.whatISee: The ego travels along the junction, turns onto the vertical roadway, and slows near the roadside blocker. A red-ringed pedestrian moves across the roadway and comes alongside the ego at the marked closest approach, after which the ego continues past.

scenarios.brief: Debris lies in the ego lane.
scenarios.name: Late-revealed lane debris
scenarios.whatISee: The ego travels along the roadway toward a lane-debris hazard while a roadside box truck remains stationary off to the side. The ego then slows sharply from 61 kph to 39 kph, nearly stops at 3 kph, and is stopped at the closest approach with the debris still ahead in its lane.

scenarios.brief: A disabled vehicle is stopped in the ego lane.
scenarios.name: Late-revealed disabled vehicle in ego lane
scenarios.whyNot: The disabled vehicle is stopped in the junction on the crossing/adjacent roadway rather than clearly in the ego's lane; it does not occupy the ego lane as required by the brief.
scenarios.whatISee: The ego vehicle travels toward the junction and slows sharply from 62 kph to 2 kph. A red disabled vehicle is stationary in the junction ahead and to the ego's right, while the yellow roadside occluder remains off to the side.

scenarios.brief: Fallen cargo blocks part of the ego lane.
scenarios.name: Late fallen cargo lane blockage
scenarios.whatISee: The blue ego vehicle drives toward a stationary object labeled fallenCargo lying ahead in its lane. As it closes on the cargo, the ego vehicle slows from 61 kph to a stop at the closest approach, leaving the cargo directly ahead.

scenarios.brief: A hazard sits just beyond a crest or curve.
scenarios.name: Late blind-curve opposing left-turn intrusion
scenarios.whyNot: The red hazard is a turning vehicle entering from a side road at the junction, not an object sitting just beyond and hidden by a crest or curve. The yellow occluders are stationary props rather than the hazard described.
scenarios.whatISee: The ego approaches a curved/junction area while yellow occluder props remain along the roadway. A red turning vehicle then enters from the side and crosses/turns through the ego's path, reaching closest approach before separating as both continue.
